pr.title: fix: NO_PROXY should support IPv4, IPv6 and localhost
pr.description:
Closes #2660

The proxy-environment parsing that builds no-proxy bypass rules always prefixed entries with a wildcard, treating every NO_PROXY entry as a domain name. IPv4, IPv6, and 'localhost' entries were not handled correctly. In particular an IPv6 entry such as '::1' was wrongly transformed into a pattern that a later URL parsing step could not interpret, causing an error. This PR handles NO_PROXY hostnames as domains, IPv4, IPv6, and localhost separately.

testCase.title: Client construction succeeds when NO_PROXY names an IPv6 loopback address
testCase.preconditions: The environment variable NO_PROXY (or no_proxy) is set to the single value '::1', the IPv6 loopback address. No other proxy-related environment variables are set.
steps: Set the NO_PROXY environment variable to '::1'.
Create a new HTTP client instance that reads proxy configuration from the environment (the default behaviour).
Observe whether the client is created successfully.
If creation succeeds, send a request to a host other than the loopback address and confirm it still goes through normally.
testCase.expectedResult: The client is created without raising any error, correctly recognizing '::1' as a host that should bypass proxying, and it can still be used to make requests normally.

provenance.note: Before the fix, every NO_PROXY entry (including IPv6 addresses) was prefixed with a domain wildcard when building the client's proxy-bypass rules, which are constructed eagerly at client-creation time; an IPv6 entry like '::1' produced a malformed rule that later URL parsing could not handle, so client creation raised an error at the base revision.

pr.title: BUG: Series.str.match raised for regex flags other than re.IGNORECASE (GH#63108)
pr.description: Follow-up to GH-63108, which added validation of conflicting case/flags/compiled-pattern arguments to Series.str.match but in doing so broke every regex flag other than re.IGNORECASE. That change compiled the pattern with the full flag set, then reset flags and derived 'case' from IGNORECASE alone, so the reconstructed flag set failed a strict equality check against the compiled pattern's flags for anything other than IGNORECASE. This restores support for flags such as MULTILINE, DOTALL, VERBOSE and ASCII, both when passed via flags= and when carried by an already-compiled pattern object, across object, string, and Arrow-backed dtypes.

testCase.preconditions: A text column contains two values: one where a newline character sits between two other characters, and one where no newline is present.

testCase.title: Default engine logging suppresses routine SQL echo output
testCase.preconditions: A database engine is created with default logging configuration and its 'echo' flag left off, and the root logger for the engine has not been given an explicit level.
steps: Attach a log-capturing handler to the engine's logger.
Execute a statement through the engine.
Turn the echo flag on and execute another statement.
Inspect what was captured at each step.
testCase.expectedResult: With echo off, no informational SQL-statement log records are captured because the effective log level only lets warnings and above through. With echo on, the SQL statement is logged.

provenance.note: logging.WARN and logging.WARNING are the same integer constant in the Python standard library, so replacing one spelling with the other is a pure rename with no behavioural effect; the effective default logging threshold, exercised by test_levels, is identical before and after.
